title: What the Python SDK's ZCC methods return, and the ones that break the tuple convention

prose.text: Most ZCC methods return the SDK's usual result, response and error tuple: [[shared.sdk-python.response-handling:tuple-return]]. The exceptions below change how a caller has to test for failure.

prose.label: Single objects and wrappers.
prose.text: {{device-details-single}} The Go SDK decodes the same call differently: [[zcc.api.devices-wire:details-response-shape]]. {{company-info-list}} {{results-wrapped-twice}} The removal calls it affects are in [[zcc.devices.removal-api]]. {{sync-raw-dicts}} The trusted-network list envelope is [[zcc.api.trusted-networks-wire:list-envelope]].

prose.label: Writes that return little.
prose.text: {{activate-empty-body}} {{python-set-kwargs}} {{add-builds-from-response}} {{add-result-has-no-id}} What the create and edit responses carry is [[zcc.api.trusted-networks-wire:mutation-response]].

checks.do: Whether the caller tested `get_web_privacy` for None rather than unpacking a tuple.
Whether a download call was wrapped in try/except, since it raises rather than returning an error.
Whether code read the new trusted network's ID from `add_trusted_network`'s result, which comes from a response with no record; list by name instead.

web-privacy-get-none.statement: `get_web_privacy` returns a bare None when the request cannot be built, when it fails, or when the body cannot be read, instead of a tuple with an error.

quotes: request, error = self._request_executor.create_request(http_method, api_url, body, headers) if error: return None
response, error = self._request_executor.execute(request) if error: return None
try: result = self.form_response_body(response.get_body()) except Exception as error: return None

web-privacy-get-dict.statement: On success `get_web_privacy` returns the camel-cased response dictionary itself, not a `WebPrivacy` model or a tuple, so it carries any non-null key the API sends, including ones the model lacks.

quotes: try: result = self.form_response_body(response.get_body()) except Exception as error: return None return result
for key, val in body.items(): if val is None: continue

device-details-single.statement: `get_device_details` builds one `DeviceDetails` object from the whole response body, treating the endpoint as returning a single object.

quotes: def get_device_details(self, query_params: Optional[dict] = None) -> APIResult[dict]:

company-info-list.statement: `get_company_info` returns a list of `CompanyInfo` objects, each built again from a result the executor already wrapped as a `CompanyInfo`; a single-object response becomes a one-item list.
company-info-list.conditions: Added that each item is wrapped twice (the executor is given the model class); the effect is results-wrapped-twice.

evidence.after: # ZCC can return either a single object or a list of objects

results-wrapped-twice.statement: `get_company_info`, `remove_devices` and `force_remove_devices` wrap each result in their model twice, so only fields whose wire key equals the attribute name survive (`name`, `udids`, `username`); `org_id`, `business_name` and `devices_removed` come back None.
results-wrapped-twice.conditions: Traced: for ZCC, `get_results()` returns model objects when `execute` is given a model class; `form_response_body` returns a non-dict unchanged; the model's `"key" in config` test is `hasattr`, so a camelCase wire key is not found on the object. Reproduced locally against the SDK models; not run against a tenant.

add-builds-from-response.statement: `add_trusted_network` returns a `TrustedNetworks` object built from the create response itself, with no follow-up lookup.

add-result-has-no-id.statement: The recorded v1 create response carries only `conditionType` and `active`, so the object `add_trusted_network` returns has no ID or name of the new network.
add-result-has-no-id.conditions: Now cites the recorded create response instead of the Go SDK's comment: one test tenant, recorded with SDK 1.9.13 (Python SDK cassette). The Python result object itself was not observed.

python-set-kwargs.statement: Python's `set_web_privacy_info` sends whatever keyword arguments it is given, camel-cased by the executor's selective ZCC conversion, so keys outside its model can be written, but it returns a model object that holds only the modeled settings.
python-set-kwargs.conditions: Added that the keyword arguments are camel-cased (OneAPI path; the legacy client camel-cases in full, zcc.sdk-python.wire-keys:legacy-client-full-camel-case).
